about: Open models the project suggests per role (one marked `want` only when the person asked for what it is for — guided/plan.js USES), with what each needs at the quantization it is served in, in GiB as the panel reads a machine: vramGB is the model file plus its vision projector, its context cache at context.at tokens and about 0.3 for the runtime; the picker adds 15% on top. rank orders them by quality (a higher rank is better; the same model at a lossless quantization has the same rank, and then the one on a single card wins). alsoFor lists the other roles the same model serves. Every entry names its sources and the day they were checked (docs/design/model-suggestions.md). Each installs through Ollama — a library tag, or hf.co/<repo>:<quant> for a GGUF on Hugging Face (its own file is under gguf, for llama.cpp) — or, where Ollama cannot run it, as a llama.cpp server for the GGUF (install kind llamacpp-hf, <repo>:<quant>, with --jinja so its own chat template carries tool calls); speech runs as the panel's own services in Docker. A newer list arrives from the project's hub only when the owner shares with the project (sharing.js); a person can also accept a model scout suggestion into this install's own overlay.

chat.label: Talking and directing the work (the agent's own model)

models.label: Qwen3.8 27B (Q8_0)
models.toolCalling: The strongest open model of its size for agent work in October 2026: Terminal Bench 2.1 73.0, SWE-bench Pro 61.7, CoWorkBench 70.7 (model card).

models.label: Qwen3.8 27B
models.toolCalling: Qwen3.8 27B: Terminal Bench 2.1 73.0, SWE-bench Pro 61.7, CoWorkBench 70.7, ahead of Qwen3.6 27B on every agent benchmark on its card; Ollama marks the tag with tools.

models.label: Qwen3.8 27B GSQ-RCO (IQ3_S)
models.toolCalling: Qwen3.8 27B quantized by IST Austria's DASLab with GSQ and RCO: task-lossless against BF16 (AIME25 100.0 and LiveCodeBench v6 85.71 as BF16, GPQA-Diamond within 0.51) at 11.8 GB, so it runs on one 16 GB card. Its Hugging Face registry entry carries no chat template of its own, so Ollama uses its built-in Qwen renderer and tool calls work (checked 2026-10-08 on the same architecture).

models.label: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B (mixture of experts)
models.toolCalling: SWE-bench Verified 73.4, TAU3-Bench 67.2, MCPMark 37.0 (model card). Only 3B parameters work per token, so it answers at a usable speed on a processor with 32 GB of memory — the one chat model suggested without a graphics card.

models.label: Qwen3.8 27B GSQ-RCO (IQ2_XS)
models.toolCalling: The 27B at 2.5 bits fits a 12 GB card: GPQA-Diamond 84.85, LiveCodeBench v6 76.57, above Gemma 4 12B (78.8, 72.0). Tool calls are not yet measured at this size, so Gemma 4 12B stays beside it as the alternative.

models.label: Gemma 4 12B
models.toolCalling: Tau2 69.0, LiveCodeBench v6 72.0, GPQA-Diamond 78.8 (Gemma 4 card); holds up better than Qwen3.5 9B on chained tool calls.

models.label: Qwen3.5 9B (IQ4_XS)
models.toolCalling: BFCL-V4 66.1 (model card), the usual pick for tool calls on an 8 GB card; at IQ4_XS it leaves room for its context on one.

models.label: Ornith 1.5 9B (Q4_K_M, llama.cpp)
models.toolCalling: A Qwen3.5 9B fine-tune strong for its size on agent work (SWE-bench Verified 70.6, MCP-Atlas 54.2 against Qwen3.5 9B's 53.2 and 46.8, model card). Its GGUF carries a chat template with tools in Qwen's XML form; Ollama's registry entry gives it one without, so it runs as a llama.cpp server with --jinja, whose own template parsed tool calls and a tool's result correctly (checked 2026-10-08 with that template on Qwen3.5 2B, the same architecture). A reasoning model: it thinks before answering.

models.label: gpt-oss 20B
models.toolCalling: Native tool calls; an alternative from another family, below the Qwen3.8 27B builds that fit the same cards.

models.label: Qwen3.5 4B
models.toolCalling: BFCL-V4 50.3 (model card): enough for simple tool calls on a small card.

models.label: Qwen3-TTS 1.7B — an expressive voice
models.note: Whispers, laughs and excitement on request, Italian and English among ten languages; measured on an RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB: 6.8 GB of graphics memory, first audio in about 50 ms, a sentence at four times real time. The image (vLLM-Omni) is an 11 GB download and 33 GB on disk; the model 4.5 GB.

watching.why: Qwen3.8 Flash Next (125B, 6B active) at 2.5 to 3.5 bits, for machines with 64 GB or more. Its split files now install (llamacpp-hf, e.g. ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF:IQ2_XS, 63 GB in two parts, each quantization in its own folder), but its architecture (qwen4exp) needs a llama.cpp built after 2026-08 and no machine the project tests on can hold it, so it has not been run yet: a suggestion once it has.
Faster than Whisper for European languages; needs a speech service row of its own before it can be suggested.
52 languages, streaming; needs a speech service row of its own.
